notes: THE MECHANISM, established before any invocation: describeCapability's contract for import_dataset_c_s_v declares exactly one input, the path param `project_id`. There is no body parameter, no query parameter, and no declared field of any kind for the CSV content itself — the endpoint's only real input is a multipart/form-data file part, and invokeCapability is a JSON-only tool (path_params/query/body, all JSON-typed). There is no key to put a byte stream, a base64 blob, or a file reference into, because none is declared. This is not a guessable gap to work around; the registry entry itself already flags it in guidance as a 'QUARANTINE CANDIDATE — do not attempt to call this,' stating plainly that any invocation from this profile fails with 400 {error:'No file uploaded'}. One invocation was made anyway (project_id only, empty body) purely to confirm that documented behavior against the live preprod API rather than take the registry's word for it: it returned exactly 400 {"error":"No file uploaded"}, matching the guidance verbatim. No second or third attempt was made — there is no alternative body shape to try when the contract declares zero fields for the file; retrying the identical no-file call would only reproduce the same 400 deterministically, and inventing an undeclared field name would be testing a guess, not the contract. The data-loss hazard this task asked to check for (an import silently replacing all rows, the way update_dataset's own minItems:1 guard prevents wiping via omission) is a non-issue for this specific capability by construction — there is no dataset reference to target, destructive or otherwise. It would become a live question only for whatever downstream capability actually consumes this endpoint's parsed {headers, rows} output to perform the real import (not present in this registry snapshot under a name probed so far). MALFORMED-CSV QUESTION: not reachable — testing mismatched column counts or a bad header requires actually sending file content, which is exactly the blocked step; the registed guidance separately documents that reachable malformed-input failures return 422 {success:false, error:...} (bad extension, blank headers, oversized file, over the 40-col/100-row standard-tier limit), but this could not be exercised live from this profile. INHERITED create_dataset CHECKS: not applicable to this capability's own contract — its declared 200 response is {data:{success,headers,rows}}, with no `variables` field and no `created_by` sub-object at all, so neither the variables-array-shape check nor the created_by nested-drift check (browserstack_user_id/group_id missing, role undeclared-but-present) has a corresponding field here to compare against; those checks apply to dataset-shaped responses (create/get/update/list-variables), and this endpoint never returns a dataset. BROADER FINDING FOR THE REGISTRY: this is a real coverage gap, not a probe failure — three other queued attachment-upload capabilities almost certainly hit the identical wall (any endpoint whose sole content-bearing input is multipart/form-data has no way to be expressed through invokeCapability's JSON-only path_params/query/body surface). Recommend either (a) marking all such capabilities non-invokable/quarantined at the registry level exactly as this one already is, so future probes don't re-discover the same wall per-capability, or (b) adding a documented base64-body escape hatch to invokeCapability if the underlying API can accept one. Also worth flagging: the capability's own name and its declared 200 schema both frame it as import/write-shaped (mode:'write', name 'import_dataset_c_s_v'), but its guidance and its actual response shape (a bare parse preview, no dataset object, no uuid) describe a pure read/validate operation with a misleading name — the real import path for CSV data is 'parse client-side then call create_dataset with variables/rows', which was already exercised and confirmed clean in create_dataset.json.
